title.narrative: FAO_Bevarande av ekosystemen i Chiquitano och Amazonas
FAO_Preservation of the Chiquitano and Amazonian ecosystems

description.narrative:
The main objective of the project "Conservation of the Amazonian and Chiquitano ecosystems through the strengthening of livelihoods and sustainable, inclusive and resilient agri-food systems to climate change" is to strengthen the agri-food systems and livelihoods of rural native indigenous communities, based on the use and comprehensive management of natural resources and environmental functions in a context of adaptation and mitigation of climate change, reduction of poverty and food insecurity.
To achieve this task, 4 components have been established: -Component 1: Public policies for the comprehensive management of forests, water and soil strengthened in indigenous and peasant communities - Component 2: Strategies and technologies for adaptation and mitigation to climate change implemented in Chiquitano and Amazonian forests in coordination with communities, subnational governments and the national government - Component 3: Strengthened livelihoods and community productive enterprises implemented under comprehensive forest management with a climate change and gender approach - Component 4 Strategies for knowledge management and communication for development with a gender and climate change approach implemented and monitored in the impacts of the project
The main beneficiaries are expected to be: -National Government (4 Ministries) -National Authorities (3 National Authorities) -2 Departmental Government -16 municipalities -150 Communities -15 Social Organizations -30 Productive Associations -12,000Households (around 51,600 people)
At the end of intervention, it is expected that: -17,500 smallholders and 150 indigenous communities have received technical assistance in resilient agriculture practices and comprehensive forest management with a focus on adaptation and mitigation to climate change for the preservation of forest ecosystems, their environmental functions and biodiversity. -At least 5 value chains (honey, açaí, chiquitana almonds, chestnuts and fishing) that integrate indigenous and peasant communities have been strengthened and are developed under non-consumptive use practices and free of deforestation, boosting local economies. -5,250 indigenous/peasant women have developed capacities and improved the conditions that contribute to their economic empowerment - productive and resilient, of which 2,000 have access to public and/or private services (technology, financial services, markets and inputs, as well as prevention gender violence, among others). -200,000 hectares of forests and forest lands under comprehensive management contribute to the conservation of biodiversity and the fixation and capture of carbon in 1,000,000 MT, as well as hydrological regulation, organic matter in soils, among others.

Projektet syftar till att på ett artikulerat sätt bidra till bevarandet av Amazonas och Chiquitanias ekosystem i Bolivia genom att stärka försörjningsmöjligheterna genom hållbara inkluderande och klimatresilienta jordbruks- och livsmedelssystem.

The project aims to in an articulated manner contribute to the conservation of the Amazonian and Chiquitano ecosystems in Bolivia, through the strengthening of livelihoods and sustainable, inclusive and climate resilient agri-food systems.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement with FAO regarding preservation of the Chiquitano and Amazonian Systems
Decision on Contribution Preservation of the Chiquitano and Amazonian ecosystems

description.narrative: The project successfully achieved 118% of its annual targets for Year 2 and 53% of its cumulative targets to date. Progress under Result 1: A 66% advancement was recorded across indicators related to sustainable forest management, biodiversity conservation, and climate change adaptation. Notable achievements include: - Completion of technical reports for two forest utilization areas covering 26,966 hectares, enabling a second cycle of sustainable logging. - Institutional strengthening of DGGDF and ABT through the modernization of the National Forest Management System (SIMB), including the development of a digital platform for managing forest use rights. - Provision of technical assistance to ten subnational governments in territorial planning, notably the formulation of a Strategic Environmental Plan for the municipality of San Miguel. - Establishment of four community agreements focused on the conservation and sustainable use of natural resources, with an emphasis on water management. - Consolidation of three community fire brigades and the creation of an additional brigade within the ANMI Madidi National Park to enhance fire prevention and response capacity. - Completion of two technical studies: one examining the role of women in the asaí value chain, and another on fireless slash-and-burn practices (Chaqueo sin fuego). The latter has been published digitally and is scheduled for physical release in collaboration with MMAyA. Progress under Result 2: Implementation of Sustainable Production Models FAO reports a 50% achievement of indicators related to the implementation of sustainable production models in agroforestry, agriculture, and livestock, promoting the ecologically responsible use of natural resources. Key advances include: - Agroforestry and Ecosystem Management: A total of 823 hectares have been incorporated into agroforestry production models, including Agroforestry Systems (SAF), sustainable agriculture, and silvopastoral practices. To reach the target of 5,000 hectares, the production of 1.4 million seedlings is underway in nurseries managed by public institutions, communities, families, and private entities. - Infrastructure Development: An açaí pulping facility was inaugurated in the Carmen Pecha Indigenous Community, located in the municipality of Ixiamas, Abel Iturralde Province, La Paz Department. - Value Chain Strengthening: Progress was recorded in three prioritized value chainshoney, açaí, and sustainable tourism: * The honey value chain produced a surplus of two tons, and a strategic alliance was established with EBA to facilitate access to international markets. Efforts also include the protection of native bee products. * In the açaí value chain, development initiatives are focused on naturally occurring stands in northern La Paz and Pando, with ongoing strengthening of three pulp processing facilities. * In sustainable tourism, the Tacana Womens Route concept is being developed as a community-based alternative to promote responsible local development. Progress under Result 3: Strengthened Environmental Governance FAO reports a 33% achievement of indicators under Result 3, which aims to enhance environmental governance through institutional support and citizen engagement, with a particular focus on indigenous communities. Notable actions include: - Support to local TCO (Tierras Comunitarias de Origen) organizations to strengthen their capacity for monitoring and managing territorial and environmental rights. - Forest fire reporting training provided to 64 journalists (16 women and 48 men) in the municipalities of San Ignacio de Velasco, Roboré, San Buenaventura, Rurrenabaque, and Cobija. - Continued development of Bolivias National Action Plan for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD), alongside a bioeconomy-focused analysis of the açaí value chain. - Preparatory discussions for a Bi-national Meeting of açaí producers, processors, and marketers in Belén de Pará, aimed at exchanging harvesting and processing technologies and establishing trade agreements for açaí and chestnuts. Progress under Result 4: Women's Participation in Environmental Decision-Making Progress under Result 4 stands at 61%. Key achievements include: - Capacity building for 18 women leaders from indigenous organizations to support their active participation in decision-making processes related to environmental management, climate change, and territorial planning. - Strengthening the role of women in beneficiary communities through their involvement in sustainable production initiatives (SAF, sustainable agriculture, and silvopastoral systems) and improved access to markets.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
